claims.text: The initial high-entropy alloy contains no pre-existing lubricious phase.
Post-synthesis heat treatment in a sulphur-bearing atmosphere induces MoS2 precipitation in the alloy.
The induced MoS2 precipitates preferentially along grain boundaries.
A controlled sulphur-atmosphere treatment promotes formation of MoS2 lamellae within the alloy microstructure.
The treatment remains tribologically effective from approximately 25°C to 600°C when sulphur exposure and the temperature profile are controlled.
Avoiding deleterious oxidation and phase instability is necessary to preserve the treatment's effectiveness.
The structural mediator consists of MoS2 grains or platelets at grain boundaries and elsewhere within the microstructure.
MoS2 has a layered structure with low shear strength.
Low-shear MoS2 lowers friction during sliding by reducing interfacial shear stress.
Reduced interfacial shear stress mitigates wear.
Dispersed MoS2 creates microscale self-lubricating zones that function over a broad temperature range.
Relative to the untreated alloy, treatment will reduce the coefficient of friction by roughly 30–50% under similar load and speed conditions.
Relative to the untreated alloy, treatment will reduce the wear rate under similar load and speed conditions.
The untreated alloy has relatively high friction and wear because it lacks an intrinsic lubricious phase.
Insufficient sulphur content prevents formation of enough MoS2 for effective lubrication.
Oxidizing operating environments can degrade the lubricious MoS2 phase and limit treatment effectiveness.
